Epist. and Erasmus Rudingerus de origine Ubiquitatis); main text in one column to the right, ending with a catchword-less last line "Fa-ber" continued on the next line "ber" at right.

l.i: Tigurinos omnes divos eiecisse è templis,
VVals-hutenses etiam è vitreis fenestris privatarum ae-dium.

main_text.l: multò ultra quingentos annos præsentia cor-
poralis corporis Christi in cœna, tribus
tanquàm columnis fundata est: 1. falsà in-
cellarius, intelligens, futilia hæc esse omnia,
Christū, quatenus creatura est, nō posse cor-
pore suo uno & eodem tempore in plurib.
& diuersis locis esse, à divina tamen natura,
in unam personā cum ipso unitam humanā
ei communicari, ut in cœna saltem sua & in
hac quidem tantùm & sola) simul esset in plu-
ribus, omnib. nimirum cœnæ suæ locis. Quæ
proprie non est παντοχρονία, sed πλυπληία. Hoc
autem anno M. D. XXIV. Jacobus Faber

page.notes: Greek words in the text are transcribed approximately; the Greek at "τοῦτο" and "πανταχοῦ"/"πλυπληρία" is partly illegible in the scan. Marginal note letters are not marked in the text. The last word "ber" stands at the right of the final line and is a continuation of "Faber".
